newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso falls 1.04 in centbank devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso falls 1.04 in centbank devaluation.

text.p: The Colombian peso ended 1.04 down at 1,000.06 to the dollar as the central bank continued its crawling peg devaluation program, interbank traders said.

Traders said small quantities of oil export earnings entered the markets but that there was very little genuine demand for dollars. The peso, they said, was pushed down as the central bank shifted the upper and lower limits of the daily floating exchange rate band.
Dealers reported 90 trades worth a total $77 million, lower than the average daily trade of $180 million.

The peso hit an intraday high of 1,000.05 and an intraday low of 1,000.15. Dealers said the lack of demand for greenbacks was likely to see the peso floating at the upper limits of the daily band for most of the week.
